messages.subject: Time missing from data sets
parts:
I am currently analysing my ActiGraph RAW data files in R, using the GGIR package and have come across a problem and wondered if you would be able to advise me on how to correct this or why this occurs.

I have managed to run my data files through R and have CSV files outputs. However, the CSV files have the first 10 minutes of initialised time removed (this time is sometimes longer in other data files). For example, my ActiLife RAW data file starts at 13:30:00 but the CSV file from GGIR starts at 13:40:00. Is there any way to correct this or can you please advise me why this happens?

Thank you for your time and I look forward to hearing from you
Ruth Brady

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Time missing from data sets
parts:
GGIR always outputs the epochs from the first integer number windows used for the non-wear detection.
So, if you set it at 600 seconds (second value in argument windowsizes) then your output will start at 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, or 50 minutes past the hour. It might be that starting the measurement at 13:30 still rounds it off to 13:40. I did this to be able to standardise the timing of epochs, which would ease merging it with other time series, and avoids confusion about the hour or day an epoch belongs to.
In short, your timestamps are not incorrect, the code simply ignores the first bit of data. Something similar happens at the very end of the measurement.
Cheers, Vincent
